source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Carrying essentially no cardiovascular effects of any kind at all once it has actually been administered to a client in labor","B":"Being considered inappropriate for use during pregnancy under essentially any obstetric circumstance a provider might reasonably ever encounter","C":"Working mainly through vasodilation as its primary hemodynamic effect on the client's maternal blood pressure once it has actually been given","D":"Has mixed alpha and beta effects, historically thought to preserve uteroplacental blood flow better, though current evidence suggests both agents are generally acceptable"}}
source_row.rationale: Ephedrine has mixed alpha and beta-adrenergic effects and was historically favored for maternal hypotension due to theoretical benefits for uteroplacental blood flow, though current evidence suggests both ephedrine and phenylephrine are generally acceptable options in this setting.
